proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: T is profinite as a topological space; a quasi-compact open W containing f(T) is made G^0-invariant; the closed map T -> pi_0(W) and the profinite clopen refinement produce finitely many affine opens U_xi whose preimages cover T, giving an affine U_0 containing f(T) per component; each component Z meeting f(T) has a rational point and is a translate of G^0, so after translation the problem reduces to G = G^0 irreducible with an affine neighbourhood U of e; the open immersion U x_k T -> G x_k T has an image that is a finite union of boxes because |U x_k T| = |U| x |T|, hence only finitely many translates U f(t)^{-1} occur, and since G is irreducible their intersection is nonempty and contains a k-rational point g, giving f(T) subset g^{-1}U (source lines 1316-1401)

core_obligations: Profinite decomposition (proof lines 1321-1357): T is profinite (01YY, 08ZX); W is replaced by a G^0-invariant quasi-compact open (0B7N); psi: T -> pi_0(W) is closed (08YD), so for affine opens U_xi containing f(F_xi) the complements psi(T \\ f^{-1}(U_xi)) give open neighbourhoods V_xi; the profinite refinement (08ZZ) yields a finite disjoint clopen decomposition V_1, ..., V_n, and U_xi cap pi^{-1}(V_i) stays affine, producing a finite disjoint union of affine opens U containing f(T).

Component reduction (proof lines 1359-1378): every component Z meeting f(T) contains a k-rational point z and equals G^0 z (0B7R); the preceding paragraph handles Z inside W; the translation identifying Z with G^0 is immediate from Z = G^0 z already established in-span (translate by z^{-1}), so the problem reduces to G = G^0 irreducible with affine neighbourhood U of e, and T is replaced by the closed subscheme f^{-1}(G^0) of the same type.

Finite translates (proof lines 1380-1401): the map (t, u) -> (u f(t)^{-1}, t) extends to an automorphism of G x_k T, so it is an open immersion; by 0B7T its image is a finite union of boxes, hence only finitely many opens U f(t_i)^{-1} occur; G irreducible makes their intersection nonempty, and Jacobson + rational closed points give g in G(k) inside it, i.e. f(t) in g^{-1}U for all t; g^{-1}U subset W by invariance of W.
proof_roadmap: Use closedness of T -> pi_0(W) and the profinite clopen refinement to cover f(T) by finitely many affine opens (proof lines 1321-1357).
Reduce component by component to G = G^0 irreducible with an affine neighbourhood of e (proof lines 1359-1378).
Force the finitely many translates U f(t)^{-1} to intersect via irreducibility and pick a rational point g, so f(T) lies in g^{-1}U (proof lines 1380-1401).
